title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
length: 135 chapters, an epilogue and introductory material
openingText: Call me Ishmael. Some years ago — never mind exactly how long — with little or no money in my purse and nothing in particular to hold my interest on land, I decided I would sail around for a while and see the watery part of the world.
about:
When a damp November settles in Ishmael’s soul, he goes to sea. This time he means to go whaling. At an inn in New Bedford he reluctantly shares a bed with Queequeg, a harpooner. The two become friends and ship together on the Pequod out of Nantucket. Only at sea does Captain Ahab tell his crew what he wants from the voyage. The white whale took his leg. He means to hunt it down.

Herman Melville had sailed on a whaler himself. He dedicated the novel to Nathaniel Hawthorne when it appeared in 1851. In the American edition, a school usher and a sub-sub-librarian get their say before Ishmael introduces himself. One looks up the word for whale. The other has gathered everything he can find about the animal, from the Book of Job to a shout from the masthead.

At sea, the storytelling changes its form just as readily. One night sailors speak across each other as if onstage. Another finds Ishmael at the helm in the light of the fires that render blubber. When he sets out to classify every whale in the world by size, he borrows his system from a bookshelf.

angleCards.title: Ahab’s obsession
angleCards.text: On the quarter-deck Ahab turns his private grievance into a common undertaking. Who agrees with him, and who simply falls silent?
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to follow the crew’s responses when Ahab asks for its loyalty.

angleCards.title: What do they see in the whale?
angleCards.text: Starbuck sees an animal acting on instinct. Ahab sees a will behind the white head. Ishmael can entertain both ideas long enough to be frightened by them.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to follow how the same whale changes from one observer to the next.

angleCards.title: Looking with Ishmael
angleCards.text: Ishmael can begin with a detail on a tool and end in the Book of Job. When do I follow him, and when does he make me doubt?
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to notice how the storyteller directs my attention.

angleCards.title: When the chase stops
angleCards.text: While Ahab wants to press on, I get time to examine a line, a fin or a coin. What do I learn about the people along the way?
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to read a technical chapter slowly enough to picture the work.

cast.name: Ishmael
cast.description: A former schoolmaster and merchant sailor, Ishmael ships on the Pequod as an ordinary seaman. He can take on the voice of a preacher, then turn a joke against himself. Notice when his first-person voice steps aside to let somebody else speak.

cast.name: Captain Ahab
cast.description: Captain of the Pequod. Ahab lost a leg to Moby Dick and walks on a replacement carved from a sperm whale’s jaw. When he nails an Ecuadorian doubloon to the mast, every hand on deck can imagine winning it by spotting the whale first.

cast.name: Moby Dick
cast.description: An enormous sperm whale that sailors know by his white hump and wrinkled brow. Ahab takes the animal’s blow as a personal attack. Ishmael spends an entire chapter exploring how whiteness can inspire both reverence and terror.

cast.name: Starbuck
cast.description: The first mate is a Quaker from Nantucket and an accomplished whaleman. He dares speak against Ahab on the quarter-deck. Later, with a loaded musket outside his sleeping captain’s cabin, he must decide what his duty to the crew demands.

cast.name: Stubb
cast.description: The second mate comes from Cape Cod, usually with a pipe between his teeth. He can talk to his oarsmen in pursuit of a whale as easily as he might talk to them at supper. His good humor can keep people going or brush their concerns aside.

cast.name: Queequeg
cast.description: Queequeg is a harpooner from Rokovoko, where his father is king. His friendship with Ishmael begins under a shared counterpane in New Bedford. On the crossing to Nantucket he goes overboard to save a man who has been making fun of him.

acclaim.quote: But it is a great book, a very great book, the greatest book of the sea ever written.

whyItMatters.title: The price of a doubloon
whyItMatters.body: Ahab nails his coin to the mast where everyone can see it. It is a reward for the first sighting of the whale, yet the sailors cannot agree on what the images stamped on it mean. In chapter 99 the coin stays still while one reading after another passes before it.

whyItMatters.title: A book of voices
whyItMatters.body: Try reading the sermon in chapter 9 aloud, then listen to the voices on the forecastle at midnight in chapter 40. In both places words set a gathering in motion. In the chapel one man has the floor. On deck it is hard for a sailor to finish even a song.

whyItMatters.title: Work at sea
whyItMatters.body: When a whale is killed, the work has barely begun. Blubber must be stripped away, hoisted on deck, minced and boiled. Watch where people put their hands and feet. A loose coil of rope can decide who gets home.
